newsitem.title: CHINA: China Three Gorges bond may be 3-year, at 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: China Three Gorges bond may be 3-year, at 11 pct.

text.p: A planned issue of bonds to finance China's Three Gorges dam is expected to have a term of three years and carry an annual interest rate of 11 percent, officials said on Saturday.
China's State Planning Commission on Thursday approved the issue of 1.0 billion yuan ($120 million) in domestic bonds to finance the giant hydroelectric project that will dam the might Yangtze river.

An official of the China Yangtze Three Gorges Development Corp that will issue the bonds said the company hoped the People's Bank of China, the central bank, would shortly approve the bonds for three years with an annual interest rate of 11 percent.
Marketing of the bonds was expected to begin soon after the Chinese Lunar New Year, which falls on February 7 this year.
The bonds would be listed in Shanghai, the China Daily on Saturday quoted the official as saying.
Income from the bonds would be used to offset a shortfall in investment in the dam project in 1996, he said.

Total spending on the Three Gorges dam project was 7.6 billion yuan in 1996, with 4.2 billion yuan coming from a special fund and 3.0 billion yuan from special loans. That left a capital shortfall of 400 million yuan, temporarily covered by the company with working capital surplus from previous years, the newspaper said.

The issue, the first by the Three Gorges corporation inside China, had been rated AAA- by the China Chengxin Securities Rating Co. The bonds were classified as corporate bonds for enterprises directly run by the central authorities.

The dam project, which officials say will cost 90 billion yuan at fixed current prices and will be finished in about 20 years, is expected to be produce a huge return during the later stages of construction, officials have said.
